Tracking the Current in
Who powers AI, who pays, and why now.
A weekly radar of the electricity behind AI compute · updated Mondays · every line links to its source
What this isAI data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, and getting it has become the hard part: turbines are back-ordered, grid connections take years, and tech companies are signing 20-year deals with nuclear plants. This board follows that story every week — who supplies the power, who pays for it, and what changed.
Where the data comes fromPublic news and company announcements, collected automatically each week for about forty companies across the power and data-center supply chain. An AI model reads each article and records the layer, the type of event, the MW and dollar figures, the location and who dealt with whom. A human analyst reviews the most important items. Every line links to its source.
How to read the numbersA power plant's capacity (nameplate MW) and a data center's demand (IT load MW) are different things and are kept apart. Dollar figures are marked as stated by the parties, reported by media, or estimated. Impact 1–5 is the model's view of how much an event changes the market. Hover any dotted term for a definition.
